title: Buried in an avalanche, the clock starts at once ⏱️
subject: avalanche
description:
Would you know which way is up? 👇

What happens to your body when an avalanche buries you? Swiss and Canadian rescue data show survival stays above 91% for about 18 minutes, then collapses as packed snow stops you breathing. In 143 Canadian deaths, not one was from cold.

Sources: Haegeli et al. 2011, "Comparison of avalanche survival patterns in Canada and Switzerland", Canadian Medical Association Journal 183(7):789-795 (Simon Fraser University; Swiss data from Brugger et al.)
tags: what happens if you get buried in an avalanche
how long can you survive under snow

scenes.text: Buried in an avalanche, you have about 18 minutes.
When the slide stops, the snow packs around you, up to five times denser than fresh powder.
It squeezes your chest so you can't fully breathe.
Swiss records show over 91% of buried people survive the first 18 minutes. By 35 minutes, only 34% do.
In Canada, doctors studied 143 avalanche deaths. 81% suffocated. Not one died of cold.
Canada's wetter snow kills faster, so Simon Fraser University researchers say dig within 10 minutes.
